cities.d: the capital and largest city of the country has a mix of modern and colonial architecture, and is the best place to enjoy Peruvian cuisine

x.around: Line 2, to run in the east-west direction toward Callao, is under construction, and is expected to open in 2024; once it's opened, the attractiveness of the metro system for the visitors is likely to significantly increase.

hidden.d: In addition to exhibits featuring the use of electricity, the museum also covers the history of Lima's trams and runs a restored tram Tu-Su 10:00-17:00. Adults S/2, children S/1.
Covers the history of the Peruvian navy. And you can walk along the promenade in front and even take a short cruise in the harbor (extra fee).
Arte Colonial.

x.intro: Lima is the best place to try Peruvian cuisine, which has a huge variety of ingredients from the coast, mountain and Amazon regions. The cold sea current that passes Peru's long coast makes the sea very rich in fish and seafood.

must.d: Showcases remarkable chronological galleries providing an excellent overview on 3,000 years of development of Peruvian pre-Columbian history.

This is the main square of downtown Lima. In the Spanish tradition, it's bordered in four sides by Government/Presidential Palace or Palacio de Gobierno, the Cathedral and Archbishop's Palace, the Municipalidad or City Hall, and…
Quite good and very didactic; the area surrounding it is worth a walk.

n.en: National Museum of Archaeology and History

n.it: Museo nazionale di archeologia, antropologia e storia del Perù

must.d: Has permanent and temporary exhibits of Peruvian art, covering pre-Hispanic, colonial, republican and modern art.

Fans of colonial churches will be pleased with the architecture of this well-known church in downtown Lima. However, the more compelling reasons to visit this cathedral include underground catacombs featuring over 25,000 real…

n.es: basílica y convento de San Francisco
Convento Máximo de Nuestra Señora del Rosario

must.d: Visited by the likes of John Wayne and Orson Welles in times gone by.

n.en: Santuario de Santa Rosa de Lima
n.es: Santuario de Santa Rosa de Lima

next.d: the "White City", in the southern highlands.
hosts an exciting carnaval every February.
The center of the Inca civilization. Luxury tourist buses run twice daily with Cruz del Sur. One of South America's most iconic sights, Machu Picchu, is just a 4-hours train ride away from Cuzco.
can be reached by taking a scenic train trip through the Andes.
a mountaineering center.
a northern city of the selva (jungle)
a desert city with an oasis called Huacachina.

x.safe: If you witness a crime being committed, do not intervene unless you are really sure of what you are doing: many criminals, even pickpockets, carry guns, knives, etc., and may use them if feeling threatened.

cities.d: a UNESCO World Heritage site that embodies a rich mix of the indigenous and Spanish colonial cultures

x.around: Prices are per ride. A ride from the main square to any place in the central district will be S/4-7. A taxi from the bus station to any hotel, S/8. From the airport, the price varies between S/20-30. Some cab drivers try to rip you off by saying prices are per head but price is always per ride for all passengers. Allow for a minor extra charge for luggage (usually half a sol per large piece).

hidden.d: Also to be found in the old countryside is the renovated centuries-old Spanish Colonial mansion Mansión del Fundador.

n.es: Conjunto arquitectónico mansión del fundador y molino de Guiñapo.

hidden.d: The Franciscan monastery was built in 1648, and distinguished by its high bell tower in red and white bricks. Four out of the original seven buildings of the monastery remain today.
A little off the usual tourist path, in downtown Arequipa. It is not as architecturally interesting as the Convento de Santa Catalina, but some of the paintings and artifacts are stunning.
A three-century-old water mill, set in the old district of Sabandia.

Around 2½ hr. Tour is more about presenting the background of Arequipa, how and why it developed into the city it is today, different aspects being presented from different locations (rather than a tour of the major sights).

Arequipa has beautiful bridges. The closest to the main square is Puente Bolognesi. Go there and visit the Tambos (ancient houses rebuilt by the city government and used as apartments). A great experience.
This 16th-century mestizo style (Andean Baroque) building was opened to the public in 1978, and is notable for its sillar walls and brick vault with a single nave.

n.en: Basílica y Convento de San Francisco de Arequipa
n.es: basílica y Convento de San Francisco de Arequipa

hidden.d: A grand two-story house in Baroque-Moorish style, built in 1773 and named after an old mulberry plant on its patio. The entrance features magnificent stone carvings, and the wooden doors inside the building are also decorated in…

x.intro: Arequipa is a city in the Southern Coastal region of Peru just below the edge of the Altiplano, at above sea level and surrounded by three impressive volcanoes. It's Peru's second most important city (after Lima), and the second most popular among tourists (after Cusco).

must.d: The first cathedral was built in 1544. This reconstruction dates from 1848, with a substantial repair after the 2001 earthquake caused the towers to collapse through the roof.

The most visited building from the Spanish era of the city. Described as a city within a city, this beautiful place with its colors, flowers and little streets will make you feel like you are back in time.

n.es: Monasterio de Santa Catalina de Siena

must.d: From May to November the main exhibit is the mummy Dama de Ampato, also known as Juanita. It is close to the main square.
Built in 1738 as the residence of general Domingo Carlos Tristán del Pozo, nowadays the building houses a branch of the BBVA Perú bank.

next.d: Theoretically possible as a day trip but not recommended; count a minimum of two days. Many people opt for at least one night in Chivay or Cabanaconde outside the Canyon, others stay in one of the…
not as visited as Colca Canyon, but surely as interesting. Cotahuasi Canyon claims to be the deepest in the world, and the mixture of wilderness, pre Hispanic ruins and Andean villages make it a…
at the head of the Valle des Volcanes is reachable by a direct (though long and bumpy) bus trip from Arequipa.

x.safe: Don't flaunt your valuables or your money; there are occasional robberies reported. Do not walk alone after 23:00 in the downtown area! All the usual advice given for Peru applies here as well. When taking standard precautions, Arequipa is a safe city, and like most of the other major Peruvian cities, there is always a fairly large police presence.

cities.d: home of the Morocucho people, a group of the Quechua

x.intro: Ayacucho is in the Southern Sierra region of Peru. Ayacucho is embedded in a broad sunny valley with mild climate. It is home of the Morocucho people, a group of the Quechua. The population is about 100,000, altitude 2,700 m.

next.d: . S/55 each for a 22-hour ride on a semi-cama bus. Buses at 06:30 and 19:00.

cities.d: well known for its fine cheeses, churches, and significance in the Spanish conquest of Peru

x.around: Taxi Seguro +51 76 365103 or +51 76 365362. Super Seguro +51 76 507090. Taxi Unidos +51 76 366438.

hidden.d: A picturesque town with waterfalls. The falls are a few kilometers from town but a fairly easy walk. There is also a farm with a lake and gardens nearby.
Natural hot springs. Take a microbus (written Baños on the side) from the start of Avenida Atahulpa for S/2 (as of 2024). Entrance S/6 (swimming S/6). Swimming pool closed on Friday.
The museum of the church of San Francisco.
A pre-Inca necropolis like Ventanillas de Otuzco but bigger and in much better condition. No touristic infrastructure at all, seldom visited.
Archaeological and ethnographic museum in the historical building of Belén.

n.es: Museo Arqueológico y Etnográfico del Conjunto Monumental Belén

hidden.d: An Evangelical farming colony with tourist services and a zoo.

n.es: iglesia y Convento de La Recoleta

x.intro: Cajamarca is in the northern highlands of Peru. The city is well known for its fine cheeses and dairy products. Cajamarca is also known for its churches, and hot springs, or Inca Baths.

must.d: The site features monolithic statues and a museum featuring ceramics, semi-precious stones and gold objects. Tours from Cajamarca are S/100, however if you can make it there on your own, the entry fee is S/4.50.

A pre-Colombian aqueduct built around 1000 BCE to bring water from the mountains to the town of Cajamarca during the dry season. Tours from Cajamarca are S/18 per person. Food and drinks are readily available at the site.
The only building left from the Inca empire in the city is this room, where the Inca Atahualpa was held captive by the Spanish conqueror Francisco Pizarro.

A pre-inca necropolis. Touristic infrastructure, entrance fee (S/5 in February 2017), info plates in English. This is easy to get to by microbus just look for any bus that has Otuzco written on the side, you'll find them easily…
This Catholic cathedral was built in the Baroque style. Construction of the cathedral began in the 17th century. It is located on the main square, the Plaza de Armas.

next.d: & the amazing fortress of Kuelap go with Virgen de la Carmen (12 hours, S/50 (2017))

x.safe: Traffic is probably the visitor's biggest risk. Most drivers assume that you will get out of their way. Driving the wrong way on a one-way street is not uncommon, but stopping at stop signs is. So, look around before you cross the street!

cities.d: a lively city with several archaeological sites and museums

x.around: Chiclayo is full of Tico taxis. Short journeys cost S/3. A station would be better if less easy to find to go to Sipán, Ferreñafe, Lambayeque or the beaches S/15, or Túcume S/20. Three wheeler motor rickshaw mototaxis cost half the price.

hidden.d: This popular public park has many statues of Greek goddesses, the muses.
A public recreational park featuring many statues of mythical significance to the pre-Hispanic Moche and Lambayeque cultures. The walking area is lined with many trees and a canal.

Archeological site with 26 pyramids built by the pre-Hispanic Peruvians. It includes a museum showcasing artifacts from the ancient Peruvians including colonial times. Tuesday to Sunday 09:00-17:00. 32 km north of Chiclayo.

x.intro: Chiclayo is in northern coastal Peru.Chiclayo is one of the liveliest cities in northern Peru. The plazas like Parque Principal or Plazuela Elias Aguirre buzz with life even after sunset.

must.d: The cathedral in Neoclassical style is the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiclayo. Pope Leo XIV, then known as Robert Francis Prevost, was Bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023 and regularly celebrated mass in the…
Combi from Terminal Epsel.

The museum is in the center of Lambayeque and definitely worth a visit although descriptions are in Spanish only. It features most of the treasures of the Sipan tombs together including a replica of the grave looked like and how…

n.fr: musée des Tombes royales de Sipán
n.it: Museo delle Tombe Reali di Sipán

must.d: Different from Sipan Museum. Museum with replica of Sicán tomb burial site discovered in 1987, exhibits remains of Sicán culture. It is 18 km north of Chiclayo in Ferreñafe.
Founded in 1921 by Hans Heinrich Brüning, the Brüning Museum showcases the main cultures of Northern Peru, such as the Mochica and Lambayeque cultures. S/8 Adults (Sep 2026)

next.d: (3 hours) & on to Lima (11 hours).
& Tarapoto.

x.safe: The bus companies, hotels & thieves are very central. Do not flash any valuables (such as taking a photo) when walking around this area; it looks safe but there are thieves around.

cities.d: one of Peru's most visited cities as it is the largest and most comfortable city from which you can begin visits to Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley, and other Inca sites in the region

x.around: The center of Cuzco is small enough to walk around, although you will probably need to catch a bus or taxi to the bus station, Sacsayhuamán or the airport. Beware about walking around at night alone or drunk as robberies have often been reported.

hidden.d: Down Av. Sol, is a statue of the Inca warrior King Pachacuteq. The statue is placed on a cylindrical base and the total monument is over 22 m high.
A great place to visit one of Cuzco's many great coffee shops. Next to the Plaza is the main market, which is fairly traditional and is a worthwhile visit.
Displays a collection of popular art featuring handcrafts of the modern era.
The ruins of an Inca palace, the home of 15th-century Inca emperor Pachakuti Inka Yupanki, which you can walk around in. The Inca and colonial stonework and architecture is interesting.
A shop ("museum") explaining the history of cacao (free) and offering chocolate workshops (not free) as well as cacao farm tours (not free).

The most distant ruin on the route from Cuzco. It is a small site with an ornamental fountain whose source is unknown as reportedly archaeologists lack the tools necessary to determine the source without damaging the site.

In the home of the Inca historian Garcilaso de la Vega, this 2-story museum has many paintings from the 17th and 18th century as well as historical displays chronicling the pre-Hispanic Inca civilization, the invasion of the…
Extensive museum of pre-Inca, Inca, and colonial artifacts. Labels in English and Spanish, though the descriptions in English are sometimes pretty different from the ones in Spanish.

x.intro: Cuzco or Cusco (Qosqo in Quechua, Cusco in Spanish), in the Southern Sierras, is a fascinating city that was the capital of the Inca Empire. Cuzco is a and is one of Peru's most visited cities as it is the largest and most comfortable city from which tourists can begin visits to Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley of the Incas, and other Inca sites in the region.

must.d: The central site of worship for the Incas. Like so many other testimonies of fantastic Inca architecture, it was severely devastated by the conquistadores, the Spanish conquerors, who built their Christian church, Santo Domingo,…

Elaborate large cathedral full of colonial-era religious paintings. The biggest church in Cuzco, in front of Plaza de Armas. As a tourist the entrance is S/25. If you go in a "misa" (mass) between 06:30–09:00, it is free.
A large stone in one wall has 12 sides and 12 angles. This one has become almost a symbol of Cusco and is a striking example of the precision of Inca architecture and stonework.

next.d: Colorful marketplace, climb up to the expansive ruins to the religious site and cemetery behind. 32 km (20 mi) from Cuzco. Accessible with the boleto turistico.
Religious center that doubled as a fortress during the Spanish conquest . A great place to visit on the return from Machu Picchu or an alternative if you don't want to visit Machu Picchu.
PeruRail connects Cuzco to Juliaca and Puno, and the journey is one of the most spectacular rail journeys in the world, passing through amazing scenery and the middle of small towns.

the atmospheric ruin perched below the Andes and above the jungle. For the best experience, walk there on the Inca Trail or one of the alternative trails, which is certainly worth the exercise! There…
like Machu Picchu a big Inca ruin area at the edge of a mountain with great view. It offers much bigger area and terraces but less housing.
a high-altitude, dramatic alternative to the treks above, without historic sites but with amazing scenery.
visiting Lake Titicaca is the perfect way to complete a journey to the Southern Andes. It is possible to travel from Cuzco taking a direct 30-minute flight, traveling by train or by road, which…
there are overnight buses direct from Cuzco to La Paz that pass through Desaguadero. The duration seems to be about 15-17 hr long.

x.safe: Law enforcement related to drugs is very severe in Peru - that is, years in prison and no pleasure. Consider that many "long resident tourists" are part of the scene. It is already a felony that you "consider to maybe accept" an offer to buy.

cities.d: gateway to some of the top national parks and reserves for ecological conservation and wildlife viewing, and for Amazon boat rides, and a destination for those who are interested in the ancient…

x.around: The most common way to move around town is by motocar (or mototaxi), a motorcycle with a small, rickshaw-like passenger cabin in the back. Regular taxis are available too, but the heat and availability of the motocars makes it advisable to take a motocar. Sometimes the S/2.5-3 ride is worth the cost just for the breeze.

hidden.d: It houses spectacled alligators, paiches (the biggest freshwater fish in the Amazon basin and one of the longest fish in the world), and the Victoria amazonica (the biggest lily-pad in the world).
Tapiche Jungle Reserve is deep inside the jungle where you can see primary rainforest and an abundance of wildlife in a natural setting. Activitues vary depending on the weather.
Fossil Creek Wildlife Reserve was created in May 2016 in the Terra Firme forests of the communities of Roca Eterna and Nuevo Union de Boyador.
Fully licensed and registered tour operator and eco-lodge that organizes all-inclusive jungle expeditions, Amazon riverboat cruises, trips to Pacaya Samiria Reserve.

Here they have a variety of monkey species (some endangered), as well as a sloth, some coatis, a pair of toucans and macaws, all of which are free to roam and go into the jungle, but are domesticated and hang around for the food.

At Pilpintuwasi you can see the complete life cycle and learn about the impressing development of butterflies. At the Amazon Animal Orphanage you can see the rescued endangered animals that were ill-treated, such as anteaters,…

n.en: Pilpintuwasi Butterfly Farm & Amazon Animal Orphanage

hidden.d: This lodge is in primary rainforest which is exceedingly rich in species of both plants and animals, offering many opportunities for observing birds (the area has almost 500 species) and many kinds of animals and plants,…
Licensed company operating since 2004 that organizes expeditions to the Amazon rainforest, to the Pacaya-Samiria National Reserve (described under "See" above) and survival trips.

x.intro: Iquitos is a city of 380,000 people (2017) in the Amazonas region of Peru. (Don't confuse it with the Department of Amazonas where Chachapoyas is located.)

intro: Peru (Spanish: Perú) is without a doubt one of the most captivating countries in South America. Home of the epic lost Inca citadel of Machu Picchu and the mind-blowing Nazca Lines, this country's unique past awakens the adventurer in travellers of all sorts. Its awe-inspiring scenery varies from the wild Amazon jungles to vast coastal deserts and the icy peaks of the Andes.

other.d: UNESCO World Heritage Site from the pre-Incan Chavin culture of around 900 BC

x.around: Attractions within the town are within walking distance, the same goes for most of the sites outside town (see the See section for individual advice).

hidden.d: Perched on a mountainside, this ruined building is rather inaccessible but you can see it from the road to Nunupata.
The central square is lined by the cathedral, town hall, shops, cafés and other businesses. It has a fountain in the middle, benches and colorful flowers and trees.
Sulfurous waters emerging from a rock formation. Pay at the ticket office, then descend a staircase towards the river.
A wall with carvings, created around 800 BCE. At the beginning of the Túpac Amaru there's a stone carved into the shape of a snake's head.

Yurac Machay means "white cave" and named so as it's in white volcanic tuff. In Yurac Macay there's a monolith similar to the one in the temple in Chavín. There's another cave nearby, the Cachi Machay.

The trail to the Shallapa viewpoint is a bridle path, continuing to the Pójoc archaeological site and the town of Putcor. The hike will take 30-60 minutes uphill and from the viewpoint you can see the town and the Chavín site.
The other archaeological site in the region, also serving as a ritual site, and with views to Mount Huantsán and the main Chavín site.
The national Chavín museum was opened in 2008 and displays artifacts from the Chavín culture. Exhibits include the Tello obelisk, carved conch trumpets (pututos) and carved stone statues and heads.

x.intro: Chavín de Huántar is a town and archaeological site from the pre-Incan Chavin culture of around 900 BC containing ruins and other artefacts. The site in the Central Andes of Peru is a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site.

must.d: The remains of the administrative and religious center of the Chavín culture is the main attraction of the town and inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List already in 1985.

n.es: Parque nacional de la Caldera de Taburiente
n.fr: parc national de la Caldeira de Taburiente
n.it: parco nazionale della Caldera de Taburiente

other.d: this UNESCO World Heritage site is one of the most familiar symbols of the Incan Empire, and is one of the most famous and spectacular sets of ruins in the world

x.around: There are no vehicles of any kind in the park, so bring some comfortable walking shoes, especially if you plan to do any of the hikes such as Huayna Picchu. No walking sticks are allowed in the main area, except for visitors who have difficulty walking; however, they are allowed on Huayna Picchu, where they help significantly with the climb, especially down. The walking sticks cannot be steel tipped ones.
x.intro: Machu Picchu is the site of an ancient Inca city, high in the Andes of Peru. At 2,430 metres (8,000 ft) above sea level, this is often referred to as “The Lost City of the Incas”, is one of the most familiar symbols of the Incan Empire, and is one of the most famous and spectacular sets of ruins in the world.

next.d: if spending the night or want a bath or another hike
Amazonas, Northeast Peru – largest pre-Inca ruins in South America
Bolivia – similar stonework, from a different civilization

other.d: considered to be the highest commercially navigable body of water in the world

x.around: You can get around by train. Tickets at http://www.perurail.com
x.intro: Lake Titicaca (Spanish: Lago Titicaca) is located on the border between northern Bolivia and southern Peru. Titicaca is the ancestral land of the Quechuas, Aymaras, Uros, Pacajes, and Puquinas. At elevation, is considered the highest commercially navigable body of water in the world.
